CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana
articles.full_content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has further intensified its coordinated field-level monitoring mechanism for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. As part of the monitoring mechanism, Flying Squads have been deployed in 34 districts across the two States for the period from 01.10.2026 to 30.11.2026, following a communication made by CAQM to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. For more details, visit: https://t.co/u3EqSC98CP https://t.co/AIZp3UdZJL
Accordingly, Flying Squads have been deployed across the identified districts of Punjab and Haryana. The deployment covers 18 districts in Punjab and 16 districts in Haryana, providing extensive field-level monitoring across the two States during the critical paddy harvesting period.
The Flying Squads will assess the ground-level situation in their respective allocated districts and coordinate closely with the concerned authorities and field-level stakeholders for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning. The teams will coordinate with farmers, Parali Protection Force, district-level authorities, State Government Nodal Officers, officers of the respective State Pollution Control Boards, CAQM Cell at SAS Nagar and the Commission. The ground situation, along with the steps taken to prevent further incidents of paddy stubble burning, will be reported to the CAQM Cell on a daily basis.
The deployment has been structured in successive phases, with Flying Squads assigned to respective districts for different deployment periods to ensure sustained field-level monitoring throughout the paddy harvesting season 2026. The district-wise deployment covers key paddy-producing districts in Punjab, including Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Firozpur, Muktsar, Bathinda, Amritsar, Moga, Mansa, Fazilka, Patiala, Ludhiana, Kapurthala, Faridkot, Barnala, Malerkotla, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar and Fatehgarh Sahib. In Haryana, the deployment covers Jind, Fatehabad, Hisar, Kaithal, Sonipat, Rohtak, Sirsa, Karnal, Palwal, Jhajjar, Kurukshetra, Ambala, Yamunanagar, Faridabad, Panipat and Hansi.
The strengthened field-level mechanism is aimed at ensuring timely assessment of the on-ground situation, close coordination among enforcement agencies and prompt preventive action to tackle stubble burning incidents during the harvesting season. The daily field-level reports from the Flying Squads will also facilitate continuous assessment of the situation by the Commission and enable coordinated follow-up with the concerned authorities, wherever required.

As part of Special Gram Sabha on Gandhi Jayanti, Jal Arpan Observed in more than 1850 Gram Panchayats Across Rural India to Strengthen Community Ownership of Rural Water Supply Systems Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
articles.full_content:
In A First, Har Ghar Jal Certificates Generated in Regional Languages issued to Gram Panchayats Through Jal Arpan module
On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and Special Gram Sabhas held across States/UTs, more than 1,850 Gram Panchayats/villages observed Jal Arpan- a key reform under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0- that places rural drinking water systems in the hands of the communities. This marked the formal handover of completed rural water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), reflecting the Mission's shift towards community-led management and sustainable delivery of drinking water services.
In a first, the Jal Arpan module also enabled generation of Har Ghar Jal Certificates in regional languages for eligible Gram Panchayats and villages. 346 Har Ghar Jal Certificates were generated for eligible Gram Panchayats and villages and issued in regional languages, making the certification process more accessible and citizen-centric while further strengthening community ownership of drinking water services. The Jal Arpan Module, now has provision of Har Gahr Jal certificate generations in Hindi, English and 17 other regional languages including Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Gujarati, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu , enabling communities to access programme information and certification in their own languages
Jal Arpan celebrations witnessed active participation of Gram Panchayats, Village Water & Sanitation Committees, frontline functionaries, women volunteers and community members across rural India. Completed rural water supply schemes, successfully commissioned following the prescribed trial run period, were formally handed over to Gram Panchayats and VWSCs for operation, maintenance and long-term sustainability. Activities such as Jal Sankalp, Jal Bandhan, demonstrations on water quality testing using Field Test Kits (FTKs), awareness programmes and recognition of community contributors were organised in several villages. The States and UTs also undertook activities related to water quality surveillance and monitoring, post monsoon water quality testing of sources to ensure the safety and reliability of drinking water services. Community-led water quality monitoring is being strengthened through the active involvement of women.
Digital governance and asset management are being strengthened under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 through Sujalam Bharat where water supply assets and piped water supply sources are being geotagged. On the same occasion, 2691 water supply assets including around 700 s ources were geo-tagged across the country. These efforts are supporting improved planning, monitoring and long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems while creating a comprehensive digital inventory of drinking water assets.

Union Minister of Jal Shakti Leads Special Gram Sabha Observance on Swachh Bharat Diwas 2026
articles.full_content:
Senior DDWS officials participated in Special Gram Sabhas across States/UTs
Union Minister Shri C. R. Patil participated in Special Gram Sabha at Majigam village in Chikhli Block, Navsari District, Gujarat on Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026. The Special Gram Sabha was also attended by Shri Naresh Patel, Cabinet Minister, Government of Gujarat, Joint Secretary & Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), Ms. Aishvarya Singh, District Collector and District Development Officer along with senior officials from State and District administration.
During the Special Gram Sabha, Union Minister felicitated sanitation workers and called upon everyone to make cleanliness a collective commitment and not merely a one-day campaign, but an integral part of our daily lives, behaviour and collective responsibility. He emphasized that we must resolve that neither will we litter, nor will we allow others to do so the same.
During his address, the Union Minister recalled the emphasis placed by Mahatma Gandhi on ‘Swachhata’ alongside ‘Swatantrata’ and mentioned how post-Independence the most significant efforts for Swachhta have been undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Under this, a nationwide Jan Andolan in the form of Swachh Bharat Mission has transformed rural sanitation scenario. This Janbhagidari for Swachh Bharat continues to drive the mission at grassroots level.
Along with other topics, discussions during the Special Gram Sabha also focused on achievements of SHS 2026, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and Swachh Seva Aankalan, the GP level annual digital self-assessment framework on which a presentation was made by JS&MD.
The Union Minister had earlier visited the “Waste to Art” exhibit of the GP that highlighted creative reuse of discarded materials, encouraging responsible waste management practices within the community.
A plantation drive was conducted under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’, during which Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil, and JS & MD, SBM(G), planted trees. All dignitaries and Gram Sabha participants together took the Swachhta pledge.
On Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026, Special Gram Sabhas were organized across rural India as a key activity under Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026. These Gram Sabhas provided a platform for Gram Panchayats and rural communities to review local sanitation and waste management efforts; discuss the outcomes of SHS 2026; review the status of four-way source segregation in line with the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026; identify and register bulk waste generators; and undertake discussions on Swachh Seva Aankalan in ODF Plus (Model) Gram Panchayats.
The Special Gram Sabha provided an opportunity and platform to undertake gap assessment and integrate relevant actions into Panchayat Development Plans, particularly GPDPs, for coordinated implementation at the grassroots.

Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authorities Growing Capacity to Accelerate Chhattisgarh’s Imports and Exports, Focus on Ease of Doing Business
articles.full_content:
Handled 8.17 million TEUs of container cargo in FY 2025-26; 53.93 percent share of container traffic at major ports
The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) continues to play an important role in India’s growing maritime trade and offers significant opportunities for industries in Chhattisgarh. In FY 2025-26, JNPA handled 8.17 million TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent units) of container cargo. This accounted for 53.93 percent of the total container traffic handled by the country’s major ports. During the same period, the port handled 102.01 million tonnes of total cargo.
During a Maharashtra visit by journalists from Chhattisgarh , JNPA General Manager Manisha Jadhav provided information about the port’s operations, trade facilities and future plans. She said the port’s focus is not only on increasing cargo handling but also on making the movement of goods faster and easier for importers and exporters, including businesses from Chhattisgarh.
A Modern Port Developed Over 37 Years
JNPA began operations on May 26, 1989. Over the past 37 years, facilities for containers, liquid cargo and other types of cargo have been expanded. The port currently has five container terminals, along with separate terminal facilities for liquid and general cargo.
According to JNPA, the port’s existing container-handling capacity is approximately 10.4 million TEUs per year. In view of growing maritime trade, continuous emphasis is being placed on better utilisation of available capacity and improving operational efficiency.
Simplified Procedures for Importers and Exporters
JNPA offers Direct Port Delivery (DPD) facilities for importers. After completing the prescribed customs procedures, eligible import containers can be transported directly from the port to a factory or another designated location. This reduces additional container handling and the need to move containers to an intermediate location.
According to available JNPA data, 72.66 percent of containers were cleared through Direct Port Delivery in FY 2023-24.
For exporters, the port provides Direct Port Entry (DPE) facilities. Under this system, export containers prepared at factories can be brought directly to the port in accordance with the prescribed procedures. Direct Port Entry accounted for 48.73 percent in FY 2023-24.
These arrangements aim to reduce unnecessary movement and handling of goods and save time in the import-export process. Such facilities can particularly benefit Chhattisgarh-based manufacturers, exporters and industrial units seeking faster access to international markets.
A Key Maritime Gateway for Chhattisgarh and Central India
JNPA is connected to the country’s hinterland through rail and road networks. Industries in Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and other states, along with Maharashtra, can benefit from this connectivity.
Chhattisgarh’s steel, minerals, agro-based, food-processing and engineering sectors can use JNPA to transport products by rail or road and ship them to internation

Press Conference on Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 held in Gangtok
articles.full_content:
The State Pollution Control Board (SPCB), Sikkim, in collaboration with the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Gangtok, organized a press conference today on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. The Rules have been notified by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and have come into effect from 1st April, 2026.
Addressing the media, Member Secretary, SPCB Sikkim, Shri N. W. Tamang, said that the Board is committed to ensuring timely and effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 in the State.
He highlighted that one of the key changes under the new Rules is the strengthening of source segregation. Under the Rules, waste generators are required to segregate waste into four distinct streams - Wet Waste, Dry Waste, Sanitary Waste and Special Care Waste. He emphasized that proper segregation at source is essential for efficient collection, processing and scientific disposal.
Shri Tamang said that implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 is not the responsibility of the Pollution Control Board alone, but requires coordinated action by every household, commercial establishment, institution, school, government office, Bulk Waste Generator, waste worker and Local Body. He appealed to every citizen of Sikkim to follow three basic principles: “ SEGREGATE – HAND OVER – DO NOT LITTER ”. He urged citizens to segregate waste at source and hand it over through the authorized collection system. He further stressed that waste must not be burnt, buried, dumped or littered on streets, in open public spaces, drains or water bodies.
The Member Secretary also emphasized that waste management does not end with collection. The ultimate objective is to ensure that waste is scientifically collected, transported, processed, recovered and disposed of with minimum environmental impact. He called for active public participation and collective responsibility to make the implementation of the new Rules effective and sustainable across Sikkim.
The press conference was attended by Shri Jigme Wangchuk Bhutia, State Mission Director SBM (Urban) and Special Secretary, Urban Development Department; Ms. Koshi Kapil, State Mission Director SBM (Grameen) and Special Secretary, Rural Development Department; Smt. Kusum Gurung, SFS, Additional Director, SPCB, along with other senior officials of SPCB, Sikkim.
